summary: Advises that the ip6.int domain is deprecated for standards-conformant IPv6 implementations. It is a best current practice document about which domain to use for reverse lookups of IPv6 addresses.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4159 says IPv6 implementations conforming to Internet Standards should stop using ip6.int for reverse DNS lookups and use ip6.arpa instead. It sets September 1, 2005 as the date from which ip6.int is discontinued for that support.

questions: what domain is used for ipv6 reverse mapping
subtitle: Discontinue ip6.int for IPv6 reverse mapping and use ip6.arpa

tldr.problem: The ip6.int domain had already been marked for phase-out as the domain for reverse-mapping IPv6 addresses to DNS names.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC advises that, as of September 1, 2005, standards-conformant IPv6 implementations use ip6.arpa and discontinue ip6.int.
tldr.outcome: The RFC also advises IANA and Regional Internet Registries about ending support for ip6.int.

today: RFC 4159 is a Best Current Practice advising that ip6.int be discontinued for standards-conformant IPv6 reverse mapping in favor of ip6.arpa.

sections.title: Deprecating the Old Domain
sections.content:
RFC 3152 had advised that ip6.int was deprecated for reverse mapping IPv6 addresses to DNS names and would be phased out in an orderly fashion. RFC 4159 says that, as of September 1, 2005, ip6.int should no longer be used for that purpose by implementations conforming to IPv6 Internet Standards.

The replacement domain is ip6.arpa, in accordance with the IANA considerations described in RFC 3596.
sections.plainLanguage: For IPv6 reverse lookups, the old ip6.int domain is discontinued for standards-conformant implementations. The RFC directs them to use ip6.arpa instead.

sections.title: Registry and Infrastructure Changes
sections.content:
The RFC advises IANA that ip6.int is no longer part of standards-conformant IPv6 support as of September 1, 2005. It also says Regional Internet Registries no longer need to maintain ip6.int delegations as part of that support from that date.

The registries are asked to work with their communities on a schedule for ending registration services for ip6.int.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo asks IANA and the Regional Internet Registries to stop treating ip6.int as part of standards-conformant IPv6 support. The registries are asked to plan with their communities how to end related registration services.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC notes that DNS spoofing of address-to-name mappings has been exploited in IPv4. It says removing the ip6.int zone from the standard IPv6 specification creates no new Internet security threats.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says discontinuing ip6.int creates no new security threats to the Internet.

references.text: Bush, R., "Delegation of IP6.ARPA," BCP 49, RFC 3152, August 2001.
Thomson, S., Huitema, C., Ksinant, V., and M. Souissi, "DNS Extensions to Support IP Version 6," RFC 3596, October 2003.
